technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Given an existing turn that PersistTurn/upsert and queryHistory succeed against, POST .../dialog with at least one valid dialog item returns HTTP 200 and totalDialogCount increases by the posted item count.

- A non-InvalidOperationException from AppendProcessingDialogAsync (for example DbUpdateException) is returned as a classified session-log error (not_found, persistence_error, validation_error, or backend_unavailable) rather than HTTP 500 with error=internal_server_error.
- When appendDialog fails, current-turn.yaml auditDialog is unchanged from before the call.
- After a failed appendDialog, a later successful completeTurn does not leave local auditDialog higher than the server-side processing dialog count for that requestId.
Implementation notes:

- SessionLogController.AppendDialogAsync only catches InvalidOperationException and maps 'not found' to 404. Other exceptions fall through to GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware as opaque internal_server_error. Widen the catch and use ClassifiedError, matching the RequirementsController BUG-TRIAGE-073 pattern.

- AppendProcessingDialogAsync uses raw SaveChangesAsync. Submit/Replace/Upsert used by PersistTurn use SaveChangesBudgetedAsync. Keep dialog persist on the same save/classification path as those sibling mutations.

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog increments auditDialog before Invoke-ReplRaw client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync. Move the increment after success, or roll it back on failure. Failsafe currently queues only timeout/503, so a 500 drops the dialog items.
- Do not treat local current-turn.yaml status=completed plus auditDialog as proof the incremental dialog POST persisted.
description: workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog is intercepted by Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog and calls client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync (POST /mcpserver/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/{requestId}/dialog -> SessionLogController.AppendDialogAsync -> AppendProcessingDialogAsync). That path returned method_invocation_error wrapping McpServerException with internal_server_error. The extracted error string matches GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware (payload.error=internal_server_error), not the controller ClassifiedError envelope, so an exception other than InvalidOperationException escaped AppendDialogAsync. appendActions, updateTurn, and completeTurn succeeded because they persist via Invoke-ReplPersistTurn (full session SubmitAsync/upsert), and queryHistory succeeded against the same cache, so the session/turn existed. Plugin still incremented current-turn.yaml auditDialog before the server call and did not roll it back; completeTurn then left local status=completed with auditDialog=3 even though the dialog POST failed.

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- workflow.failsafe.drain replaying client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync must use a timeout at least as large as the non-drain SubmitAsync budget (REPL_TIMEOUT, or a dedicated drain timeout), not a hardcoded 2 seconds.

- A failsafe SessionLog record whose SubmitAsync completes within the configured drain timeout must be replayed and removed from the live queue, not aborted with 'backend unreachable: mcpserver-repl timed out after 2s'.
- An explicit workflow.failsafe.drain of a payload that succeeds outside drain (observed ~73s with REPL_TIMEOUT=90) must not classify that latency as backend unreachable.

- Automatic/nested drain must still avoid blocking an in-flight getFr/getTr caller for a long SubmitAsync (preserve TR-MCP-PERSIST-003 via deferral or an equivalent non-blocking path, not a 2s timeout that cannot succeed).
- A timeout abort during drain must leave drainAttempts unchanged so a later successful pass can still replay the record.
Implementation notes:

- The smoking gun is Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds: if ($script:ReplFailsafeDraining -and $Method -eq 'client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync') { return 2 }. Both Invoke-WorkflowFailsafeDrain and Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccessCore share Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, so the cap hits operator drain and automatic drain.

- Do not reuse the 2s cap as the nested-drain safety valve. ReplRawInFlight / ReplFailsafeDrainDeferred already defer drain so it does not sit inside getFr/getTr. Raise or remove the drain-specific SubmitAsync timeout and keep that deferral.

- Default non-drain timeout is still 30s unless REPL_TIMEOUT is set. Observed successful submit was 73s, so drain should use REPL_TIMEOUT, REPL_HELPER_TIMEOUT, or a dedicated REPL_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT large enough for real session-log payloads.
- Test-ReplFailsafeBackendUnreachable matching 'timed out' is correct for a true transport failure; the bug is the artificial 2s budget producing that timeout on a reachable backend.
description: workflow.failsafe.drain sets ReplFailsafeDraining, then Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 returns a hardcoded 2 seconds for client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync. Invoke-ReplRawCore kills the REPL after that budget and returns 'mcpserver-repl timed out after 2s'. Test-ReplFailsafeBackendUnreachable treats 'timed out' as backend unreachable, so the pass aborts after one record and leaves drainAttempts at 0. The same payload submitted outside drain with REPL_TIMEOUT=90 completed in 73s. The 2s cap was meant to keep a nested drain from blocking getFr/getTr (TR-MCP-PERSIST-003), but it also applies to the operator drain verb and to deferred automatic drain, so live SessionLog failsafe records cannot replay.

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- Sequential client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync of real failsafe session_submit payloads does not return HTTP 503 backend_unavailable while the process is up and /health remains Healthy with storage reachable.
- When SaveChanges hits lock, busy, or the 5s StorageCommandBudget without a connection-class outage, the response is not backend_unavailable (busy/retryable persist, not storage-down).

- workflow.failsafe.drain replays a session_submit that takes longer than 2s (observed 73-88s, leftover 76s) without aborting as backend-down and without leaving the YAML stranded after storage answers.

- A 503 backend_unavailable burst leaves failsafe YAML on disk and a later in-process drain with storage answering replays it (no drainAttempts increment, no completed latch, no quarantine for this abort).
- /health nonce echo and overall Healthy stay as liveness-only; if writes are 503 because storage is actually down, the health payload storage field is unreachable.
Implementation notes:

- Do not treat this as BUG-TRIAGE-167 / SQL error 19 classification. Observed code is backend_unavailable (StorageCommandBudgetExceededException, RetryLimitExceededException, or connection-class SqlException), returned by SessionLogController.ClassifiedError or GlobalExceptionHandlerMiddleware.

- Root overlap with sessionlog-remediate-001 RC1/RC4: plugin still POSTs a full UnifiedSessionLogDto; SessionLogService.FindExistingSessionAsync is unbounded; only SaveChangesBudgetedAsync is 5s. Prefer incremental persist (AppendDialogAsync) and/or busy-timeout/retry over raising the 5s budget blindly.

- Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds returns 2 when $script:ReplFailsafeDraining and Method is client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync (TR-MCP-PERSIST-003: do not block getFr/getTr). Large records must drain on a long-timeout background path, not the 2s in-request walk.

- FR-MCP-FAILSAFE-001 / FR-MCP-SESSIONPERSIST-002 already require 503 degrade-queue and drain retry after storage answers; this incident is the live proof that 2s drain plus full-session upsert cannot meet that.
description: Out-of-band replay of Grok session_submit failsafe YAML (drain hardcodes a 2s SubmitAsync timeout in Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds while ReplFailsafeDraining) posted 41 records, many taking 73-88s, then 11 consecutive client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync calls failed with method_invocation_error HTTP 503 code backend_unavailable starting 2026-08-21T14:56:02Z. /health later echoed a nonce and stayed Healthy (TR-MCP-HEALTH-003 liveness; storage-only faults do not flip overall status). Remaining YAML stayed on disk until a later 120s-timeout replay succeeded (first leftover 76s for GrokCode-20260818T182741Z-plugin-session, then 1s). This is a live write-path burst, not the SQL error 19 classifier gap. SubmitAsync still full-graph upserts (FindExistingSessionAsync loads turns/actions/tags/dialog/commits unbounded; only SaveChangesAsync is under StorageCommandBudget 5s). Budget expiry and RetryLimitExceededException map to retryable backend_unavailable, so slow or contended saves look like storage-down while liveness stays Healthy. Drain cannot self-heal these payloads.

technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- After user-prompt-submit reports turn-opened for a requestId, either the session store contains that turn or the hook does not report turn-opened; a queued/degraded beginTurn must be surfaced as degraded rather than a durable open.

- When current-turn.yaml is in_progress for a requestId that the store does not have, workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog must not return HTTP 404 not_found with failsafe refused. It must recover by persisting the missing turn then appending, or retain a replayable failsafe envelope, and the dialog items must not be lost.
- A Codex prompt-submit that logs beginTurn queued/degraded followed by appendDialog must still produce durable dialog (store or failsafe) for that requestId.
Implementation notes:

- plugins/core/lib-ps/plugin-hook.ps1 Open-PluginTurn reports turn-opened after beginTurn exit 0 and current-turn.yaml matching the new requestId. It does not inspect LastReplPersistenceDetails.degraded/queued.

- plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 Invoke-WorkflowBeginTurn writes current-turn.yaml, then Invoke-ReplPersistTurn. Timeout/503 sets degraded queued failsafe-queue and Complete-ReplBeginTurnAfterPersist returns ok=true with current-turn left in_progress, so beginTurn returns true.

- Invoke-WorkflowAppendDialog uses incremental POST client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync. Combined output matching not_found|HTTP 404 logs 'turn not found (retryable false); failsafe not used' and returns false without Write-ReplFailsafe. Timeout/503 is the only appendDialog failsafe path.

- Fix at the seam: do not advertise a store-backed open until SubmitAsync (or failsafe drain) creates the turn; and/or on appendDialog 404, re-submit the cached turn then retry dialog (or queue a combined failsafe) instead of refusing persist.
description: user-prompt-submit (Open-PluginTurn) treats workflow.sessionlog.beginTurn as success when persist is queued/degraded. beginTurn writes current-turn.yaml before SubmitAsync, then returns true on timeout/503 while the failsafe session_submit envelope is retained and the turn never lands in the session store. The hook still emits status turn-opened for that requestId (example req-20260904T022234Z-prompt-36ed). Later workflow.sessionlog.appendDialog posts client.SessionLog.AppendDialogAsync against the cached requestId, gets HTTP 404 not_found, and explicitly skips failsafe (retryable false). technicalDetails: Acceptance criteria:

- The completed persist payload includes a non-empty queryText recovered from cached queryTitle, or a recovered placeholder when both queryText and queryTitle are missing, and does not fail with a QueryText ParameterBindingValidationException.
- After CompleteTurn succeeds, the cached turn is no longer in_progress, so a later beginTurn or CompleteTurn does not keep operating on the stale requestId.
- Superseding that same queryText-less in_progress turn from beginTurn still persists the prior turn as canceled instead of dropping the persist with the same empty-QueryText bind failure.
Implementation notes:

- Failure site: plugins/core/lib-ps/Invoke-McpPlugin.ps1 CompleteTurn -> plugins/core/lib-ps/final-response.ps1 -> Invoke-WorkflowCompleteTurn in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1. Upsert builder is New-McpPluginTurnUpsertRequest in plugins/core/lib-ps/McpPluginShim.psm1 (QueryText is Mandatory, Title already has AllowEmptyString).

- Cover the missing-queryText CompleteTurn and supersede paths in PluginPowerShellRuntime tests; existing fixtures always seed queryText so this gap is untested.
description: Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin CompleteTurn routes through final-response.ps1 to workflow.sessionlog.completeTurn. That path omits queryTitle unless the caller supplies it (TR-MCP-REPL-015), then Invoke-ReplTurnUpsertParams fills QueryText from Get-ReplCurrentTurnQueryText and falls back only to that empty title. The failed close leaves the in_progress turn in cache, so later work can attach to the wrong turn. The C# SessionLogWorkflow already recovers QueryText from QueryTitle or 'Recovered session-log turn'; the plugin persist path does not.

- Investigate live subscriber reject cause for txn-0c488a1a6c48404d861edbdecaa5a2ea: InMemorySubscriberCommitService can reject on verify failure, encrypted-body hash mismatch, decrypt failure, stale sequence, replay nonce, or duplicate conflict; the coordinator also maps publish exceptions to SubscriberUnavailable and commit deadline to CommitTimeout.
description: Native sessionlog_begin_turn for Codex-20260915T201211Z-r0-parity / req-20260917T134022Z-existing-gigdriving-app failed as nonretryable internal_server_error. FR-MCP-REPL-011.description: BUG-TRIAGE-097. The MCP plugin PowerShell runtime writes every session-log submit to a failsafe queue on disk before calling the backend, so a crash or an unreachable server cannot lose the turn. Until now nothing ever replayed those records: the queue only grew, and plugin Status reported pendingCount 0 while captured turns sat undrained (33 records in F:/GitHub/McpServer as of 2026-07-20, oldest 2026-07-14, eight added in a single session). Plugin Status MUST report the real queue depth.

A backend-rejected record does not block newer records, and a structurally unreplayable or exhausted record is quarantined with diagnostics rather than deleted or retried forever.
Plugin status reports the real pending and quarantined queue depth for the active workspace and agent.

Drain submission uses the 120-second default helper budget and honors a larger REPL_TIMEOUT; an ordinary two-second nested helper budget is not applied to replay. Automatic nested drain defers while a REPL call is in flight and a timeout abort leaves drainAttempts and completion latch unchanged.

TR-MCP-REPL-016.description: BUG-TRIAGE-097. The plugin PowerShell runtime captures every session-log submit into the failsafe queue before the remote call but never replays it, so records accumulate forever (33 on disk in F:/GitHub/McpServer, oldest 2026-07-14). plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST expose Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, which walks the failsafe directory oldest-first (the file name is prefixed with the UTC capture stamp, so a name sort is a chronological sort) and re-issues each record's captured method and params through Invoke-ReplRaw. A record MUST be deleted only after its submission succeeds; a record whose submission fails MUST stay on disk. client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync is an upsert keyed by sessionId plus requestId, so a replay is idempotent. A record rejected by the backend MUST NOT block the newer records behind it: the drain increments that record's drainAttempts counter and continues the walk. A transport-level failure (MCP_UNTRUSTED, mcpserver-repl not on PATH, timeout, refused connection) MUST abort the pass without consuming any attempt budget, because the backend and not the record is at fault. The drain MUST skip the record belonging to the submit currently in flight, so a drain triggered inside an active submit cannot double-submit or delete the live turn. The drain MUST be wired to the first successful Invoke-ReplRaw in the process (Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccess, latched to run at most once and disabled by MCP_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_DISABLED=1) rather than to bootstrap: bootstrap only proves the marker file is fresh, does not prove the backend answers, and runs inside Invoke-ReplRaw, so draining there would recurse. Operators MUST be able to force a full pass with the plugin-local verb workflow.failsafe.drain (optional maxRecords and maxAttempts params), which prints the drain summary as YAML and exits non-zero only when the pass aborted.
TR-MCP-REPL-016.title: Failsafe queue drains oldest-first after a proven-reachable backend call

TR-MCP-REPL-017.description: BUG-TRIAGE-097. A failsafe record that cannot be replayed MUST be quarantined rather than retried forever or deleted, because a captured record can be the only copy of a turn. plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST move a record to a quarantine subdirectory of the failsafe directory, next to a sibling .reason.txt naming the quarantine timestamp, the original path, and the reason, when the record is not readable YAML, when its root is not a mapping, when it has no method or no params, or when its drainAttempts counter has reached the attempt budget (default 5). Quarantined records MUST NOT be counted as live queue depth. plugins/core/lib-ps/resolve-cache-dir.ps1 MUST own the single resolution of the queue location (Get-McpFailsafeDir and Get-McpFailsafeQuarantineDir, honouring MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR then MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR then the workspace cache) so the writer, the drain, and the status reporter cannot disagree. plugins/core/lib-ps/mcp-status.ps1 MUST count the failsafe directory: pendingCount previously counted only the cache pending directory and therefore reported 0 while 33 captured submits sat undrained, so pendingCount MUST be the sum of pending turn records and queued failsafe records, and the status document MUST additionally expose pendingTurnCount, failsafeDir, failsafeCount, and failsafeQuarantineCount. A read-only workflow.failsafe.status verb MUST report the same depth without replaying anything.
TR-MCP-REPL-017.title: Failsafe quarantine and truthful pending queue depth in plugin status
